captures.q: What are the arguments in “The Metaphysics of Sigil I — The Full Splice: Theophrastus, On First Principles, entire and in its own order, with Metaphysics Λ joined at eleven points (the edition, seated)” by Sigil? Ground your answer in a reading of the text itself.
captures.description: THE SPLICE READ JOIN BY JOIN, THEN H3; A VERDICT WITHDRAWN ON ITS OWN GROUNDS: asked for the arguments of the Full Splice, grounded in the text, ChatGPT reads #1667 (chips: Goodreads, Alexanarch, Plato Online, the Stanford Encyclopedia) as an order of inquiry, tabulates the eleven joins, quotes the Greek at them (ἔστι τι ὃ οὐ κινούμενον κινεῖ; ἐπεισοδιώδη τὴν τοῦ παντὸς οὐσίαν ποιοῦσιν; κινεῖ δὴ ὡς ἐρώμενον) and keeps the claim at its scope: not authorship, dates, or composition. Over four further turns, blank in the paste, it reads the joins for coherence under their own headings ('the account itself', 'the premise of the count', 'matter as the third thing'), then H3 (#1597) from that edition's audits (the two printed dependency violations, the continuity trial, the underpowered short-word test), gives a verdict — 'separate works first, H3 as a second reading' — and then withdraws its reason: 'I withdraw the claim that the texts make more sense separately on the grounds I originally gave.' The question it restates is comparative explanatory power, and it holds that a more coherent construction would not establish original unity.
